lessons.title: Latency distributions and percentiles
lessons.objective: Describe a service's latency with percentiles instead of an average, and predict how tail latency grows when one request fans out to many backends.

fnd-percentile-latency.name: Latency percentiles
fnd-percentile-latency.def: The pth percentile latency is the response time that p percent of requests finish within; p50 is the median and p99 describes the slowest 1 percent.

fnd-tail-amplification.name: Tail amplification under fan-out
fnd-tail-amplification.def: When one user request waits for many backend calls, the chance that at least one of them is slow grows with the number of calls, so backend tail latency becomes typical user latency.
